subject: SLA amendment request: availability carveouts & monthly credit cap (CloudNova pilot)
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika@cloudnova.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Request: SLA availability carveouts for CloudNova pilot

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile, but our ops group asked me to open a quick conversation about the SLA language before we move to signature. There are two specific asks from CloudNova for the pilot:

1) Scheduled batch maintenance windows: we run a global nightly batch (UTC 05:00-07:00) that will cause predictable 1.5–2 hour service interruptions in our region. We’d like those windows to be carved out of the uptime calculation for the 3‑month pilot.

2) Monthly credit cap: for pilots we try to cap vendor credits to 5% of the monthly bill to avoid aggressive credit triggers while we stabilize. Your standard template caps credits at 10% — would Redwood consider 5% for the pilot?

We’ve attached a simple network diagram that shows where the batch jobs hit Redwood endpoints. If needed I can loop in our infra lead (ops@cloudnova.com).

Goal is to get an amendment we can sign this week and start the pilot next Monday.

Best,
Anika Rao
Director, Cloud Operations
CloudNova

Subject: Re: Request: SLA availability carveouts for CloudNova pilot

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear notes and the diagram. Really glad the latency looked good. Quick response with a proposed compromise so we can move fast:

- Uptime target: Redwood standard is 99.95% for production. For the 3‑month pilot we can keep 99.95% but explicitly carve out scheduled maintenance matching your nightly batch window (UTC 05:00-07:00) provided it is defined in writing and notified 72 hours in advance.

- Monthly credit cap: we can agree to a reduced cap of 5% for the duration of the pilot. After the pilot period the standard cap (10%) would apply unless both parties agree otherwise.

- Measurement: availability will be calculated per region on our metrics dashboard; we’ll provide weekly reports during the pilot.

I’m attaching a short amendment draft with the language above. If that sounds reasonable I’ll loop in Legal (Laura Bennett) and CS (Marissa) to make sure the carveout and reporting language are operationally safe.

Next steps: confirm the pilot carveout + 5% cap and I’ll send a DocuSign with the amendment; if you prefer a 1:1 to finalize we can do 30 minutes tomorrow.

Thanks —
Priyom
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

- We can accept a scheduled maintenance carveout for a defined, recurring 2‑hour nightly window, provided CloudNova publishes the recurrence and there’s a single engineering contact for emergency changes. We’ll require 72 hours advance notice for any deviations.

Suggested addition to amendment: a weekly operational report (automated) for the pilot that lists scheduled maintenance events, measured availability, and any remediation activities.

Happy to draft that operational paragraph.

Quick legal read — below are the items I would add / clarify in the amendment:

1) Definitions:
- "Scheduled Maintenance": time windows agreed in writing in which Customer‑initiated or agreed maintenance activities occur, with a minimum 72‑hour advance notification requirement.
- "Availability": percentage of successful requests measured against the metric redwood.availability.<region> during the billing period excluding Scheduled Maintenance windows.

2) Credits formula (pilot):
- For the pilot only, monthly service credits shall be calculated as: ((Target Availability - Measured Availability) / Target Availability) * Monthly Service Fees. Credits shall be payable as a credit against future invoices and shall be capped at 5% of the Monthly Service Fees for the pilot period (three months).

3) Post‑pilot: Unless the parties execute a renewal amendment, the standard SLA credit cap of 10% will apply following the pilot.

4) Audit & Evidence: Customer may request supporting telemetry for an availability claim; Redwood will provide requested telemetry within 10 business days in a mutually agreed format.

5) Exclusions: clarify events outside Redwood’s control (e.g., third‑party cloud provider interruptions, customer misconfiguration) and that such events will not count toward Redwood’s availability calculation.

I redlined the draft SLA amendment and saved as SLA-Amendment-CLD-2027.pdf. Two small asks: confirm the exact recurrence/timezone for the nightly batch (you noted UTC 05:00-07:00 — is that fixed?), and confirm whether CloudNova wants dedicated routing (we can propose an addendum fee).

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
